title: Binary Gap
summary: Determine the greatest gap between any two consecutive ones in the binary representation of a positive integer.
statement: Determine the greatest gap between any two consecutive ones in the binary representation of a positive integer. If no such gap exists, return zero. The gap is measured by the absolute difference in their positions, where the least significant bit is at position 0.
constraints: Return the largest distance between consecutive one bits, or zero if fewer than two.
hints: Only positions of consecutive set bits matter.
Scan bits while storing the previous one-bit index.
On each one update max(index-last), then set last=index.
Each adjacent pair of set-bit positions is considered exactly once.
editorial: Each adjacent pair of set-bit positions is considered exactly once.

tests.explanation: Binary 10110 has consecutive-one distances two and one, so the maximum is two.
Binary 1000 has one set bit, so the answer is zero.
